conclusion: Re-transcription with the same Whisper setup does NOT help. 0 of 30 sampled rows became confidently labelable: 28 are near-identical to the original (median similarity 0.98, 9 exactly identical) and the remaining 2 only changed dialect register, not clarity. The still-garbled rows came back as different word salad, equally unlabelable. The garbling lives in the audio (Egyptian dialect + noise + short clips), not in the decoder, so re-running the same model on all 219 would reproduce the same transcripts at ~2.5 hours of CPU for nothing. Recommendation: EXCLUDE the 219 from training (keep them out, do not train on best-effort labels). If the team wants to rescue any of them, the next test should be a genuinely different approach (VAD filtering, different decoding settings, or human listening), not a same-model rerun.
